description: The real past before the simulated futures begin in 2027: real technologies (at the year they first appeared, with who made them) and familiar real events they made possible. Technologies with a gameTechId are the game's own technologies; the rest exist only in the prologue. Event years carry the month as a fraction so events of one year keep their order.

techs.label:
DEEP REINFORCEMENT
LEARNING
techs.note: Neural networks that learn by trial and reward; DeepMind's Atari-playing DQN, published in Nature in 2015.

techs.label:
BEHAVIORAL
MACHINE LEARNING
techs.note: Psychographic profiles of voters built from social-media data, used for targeted political advertising in 2016.

techs.label:
TRANSFORMER
ARCHITECTURE
techs.note: "Attention Is All You Need" (2017): the self-attention architecture behind every modern language model.

techs.label:
SPARSE MIXTURE
OF EXPERTS
techs.note: Sparsely-gated mixture-of-experts layers (Google, 2017): only part of a huge network runs for each input.

techs.label:
SCALING LAWS
& COMPUTE
techs.note: OpenAI's scaling-law paper and GPT-3 (2020): capability rises predictably with model size, data and compute.

techs.label:
MOLECULAR
MACHINE LEARNING
techs.note: AlphaFold 2 predicts protein structures at near-experimental accuracy (CASP14, 2020).

techs.label:
RLHF &
CONSTITUTIONAL AI
techs.note: Reinforcement learning from human feedback (InstructGPT, 2022) turns a raw language model into an assistant.

techs.label:
GENERATIVE AI &
DIFFUSION MODELS
techs.note: DALL-E 2 and Stable Diffusion (2022): photorealistic images, and soon voices and video, from a sentence.

techs.label:
ADVANCED
SEMICONDUCTOR DESIGN
techs.note: 3-nanometre chips enter mass production at TSMC (December 2022); NVIDIA's H100 ships the same year.

techs.label:
FRONTIER
LLM SYSTEMS
techs.note: GPT-4 (March 2023): a frontier model that passes professional exams.

events.label:
AlphaGo Beats
Lee Sedol
events.note: March 2016, Seoul: DeepMind's AlphaGo defeats the Go champion Lee Sedol four games to one. Move 37 of game two had never been played by a human.

events.label:
The Cambridge
Analytica Scandal
events.note: March 2018: data harvested from up to 87 million Facebook profiles was used to target voters. Facebook's founder testifies before the US Congress.

events.label:
AlphaFold Cracks
Protein Folding
events.note: November 2020: AlphaFold 2 solves a fifty-year-old grand challenge of biology at the CASP14 assessment.

events.label:
US Chip Export
Controls on China
events.note: October 2022: the United States bars the export of advanced AI chips and chipmaking tools to China.

events.label:
ChatGPT
Launches
events.note: 30 November 2022: ChatGPT is released; it reaches an estimated 100 million users in two months.

events.label:
The Pause
Letter
events.note: March 2023: an open letter signed by thousands calls for a six-month pause on training systems more powerful than GPT-4.

events.label:
Hollywood Strikes
over AI
events.note: May to November 2023: screenwriters, then actors, strike; protection from generative AI is a central demand.

events.label:
The Bletchley Park
AI Safety Summit
events.note: November 2023: 28 countries, including the United States and China, sign the Bletchley Declaration on frontier AI risk.

events.label:
The Deepfake
Biden Robocall
events.note: January 2024: a cloned voice of President Biden tells New Hampshire voters not to vote in the primary.

events.label: The EU AI Act
events.note: March 2024: the European Parliament adopts the first comprehensive AI law, with rules for general-purpose models.

events.label:
Nobel Prizes
for AI
events.note: October 2024: the chemistry prize goes to AlphaFold's creators (with David Baker); the physics prize to Hinton and Hopfield for neural networks.

events.label:
The DeepSeek
Shock
events.note: January 2025: DeepSeek-R1, a cheaply trained Chinese mixture-of-experts model, rivals the best American systems; NVIDIA loses about $590 billion of market value in one day.

events.label:
The Stargate
Project
events.note: January 2025: OpenAI, SoftBank and Oracle announce up to $500 billion for AI data centres in the United States.
